official_sources.title: GDAL geotransform tutorial
official_sources.finding: GDAL defines the six-coefficient affine pixel/line to georeferenced transform, with pixel/line coordinates spanning from the upper-left corner at (0,0) and the first pixel center at (0.5,0.5); north-up rasters normally have negative GT(5).
official_sources.limitation: Forward affine semantics alone do not define the project boundary tie policy.

official_sources.title: GDALGeoTransform inverse transform
official_sources.finding: GDALGeoTransform can invert a standard affine transform and explicitly reports failure when the transform is uninvertible; coordinate-to-pixel addressing must therefore record inverse success and coefficients rather than assume inversion is always valid.
official_sources.limitation: Invertibility does not prove source CRS or target parcel correctness.

official_sources.title: GDAL RasterBand floating window reads
official_sources.finding: GDAL ReadRaster accepts floating-point window offsets and sizes, requires the requested window to remain inside raster bounds, can resample into a differently sized buffer, and may perform datatype translation with rounding or clamping.
official_sources.limitation: A successful read does not prove that floating windows or resampling are acceptable for terminal native-cell sampling.

official_sources.title: GDAL Dataset RasterIO bounds and overview selection
official_sources.finding: GDAL Dataset RasterIO requires integer windows within raster bounds and may automatically select overviews when decimating to a smaller buffer, so terminal reads must keep native window and buffer dimensions explicit.
official_sources.limitation: The exact driver may optimize differently; terminal policy must verify no derived overview was used.

official_sources.title: gdal_translate srcwin and projwin semantics
official_sources.finding: gdal_translate distinguishes pixel/line -srcwin from georeferenced -projwin; out-of-bounds handling can fill values unless error options are enabled, and nearest-neighbor projwin may expand to pixel boundaries. GDAL 3.11 also changed how projwin extents are transformed.
official_sources.limitation: CLI extraction behavior must not silently define the project's canonical pixel-membership rule.

official_sources.title: gdaltransform inverse mode
official_sources.finding: gdaltransform supports explicit inverse transformation and requires coordinate operations to account for source and target axis order, reinforcing that reverse coordinate mapping is a first-class audited operation.
official_sources.limitation: This tool can also use GCP/RPC/geolocation models not applicable to a plain affine DTM unless explicitly selected.

official_sources.title: NumPy floor semantics
official_sources.finding: NumPy floor returns the greatest integer less than or equal to the input; for negative fractional values it differs from truncation toward zero, which matters when inverse coordinates fall just outside the raster origin.
official_sources.limitation: Floor is a numeric primitive, not automatically the correct project boundary policy.

official_sources.title: NumPy trunc semantics
official_sources.finding: NumPy trunc discards the fractional part toward zero, producing different results from floor for negative coordinates; implicit casts or truncation can therefore address a different pixel near the upper/left boundary.
official_sources.limitation: The project should normally reject accidental truncation rather than choose between functions after observing results.

official_sources.title: NumPy ceil semantics
official_sources.finding: NumPy ceil returns the smallest integer greater than or equal to the input, supporting explicit half-open window end calculations where upper bounds require a separately defined rounding rule.
official_sources.limitation: Ceil does not establish inclusive/exclusive parcel-edge membership by itself.

official_sources.title: NumPy nextafter adjacent float probe
official_sources.finding: NumPy nextafter returns the next representable floating value toward a requested direction, enabling one-ULP probes immediately inside and outside pixel or raster boundaries.
official_sources.limitation: ULP probes are QA diagnostics and cannot be used to nudge authoritative coordinates silently.

official_sources.title: NumPy searchsorted left/right interval semantics
official_sources.finding: NumPy searchsorted distinguishes left and right insertion rules, making half-open interval ownership explicit when coordinates land exactly on sorted grid boundaries.
official_sources.limitation: Searchsorted requires a monotonic boundary array and a project-defined side policy.

official_sources.title: NumPy ravel_multi_index boundary modes
official_sources.finding: NumPy ravel_multi_index converts row/column indices to flat indices and defaults to mode=raise, while wrap/clip can silently remap out-of-range coordinates; exact raster identity should retain raise behavior and explicit C/F order.
official_sources.limitation: Flat-index identity depends on raster shape and order being immutable.

official_sources.title: NumPy unravel_index order semantics
official_sources.finding: NumPy unravel_index maps flat indices back to coordinates and distinguishes C and Fortran order, so round-trip row/column identity requires the same explicit linearization order.
official_sources.limitation: Round-trip indexing does not prove the pixel belongs to the parcel.

official_sources.title: NumPy sorting and searching routine catalog
official_sources.finding: NumPy documents distinct stable sorting, searching, arg-extrema and index-selection primitives; reproducible addressing must pin the exact primitive rather than rely on interchangeable-looking behavior.
official_sources.limitation: Library primitive identity is only one layer of the complete geospatial provenance chain.

official_sources.title: NumPy digitize bin edge semantics
official_sources.finding: NumPy digitize exposes right=False/right=True interval ownership and can return indices outside the valid bin range for out-of-range values, demonstrating why exact grid-edge ownership and bounds checks must be explicit.
official_sources.limitation: Digitize is a QA analogy/helper, not a replacement for the affine inverse transform.

official_sources.title: GDAL exact window error controls
official_sources.finding: GDAL -epo/-eco can force errors for partially or completely out-of-raster windows instead of filling values, supporting fail-closed target-window validation before any elevation sampling.
official_sources.limitation: The runner must still bind these semantics to the exact target raster and parcel.
